claims.text: With Redis down, every product read becomes a PostgreSQL query and holds one of the api's database connections; the api can keep only a limited number open, and POST /api/v1/orders needs them too, so orders can wait for one.

claims.text: A sensitivity point is a decision or setting one quality attribute depends on strongly; a trade-off point is a sensitivity point for two or more attributes at once, where moving it improves one and worsens another.

Raising the catalog-reads permit limit lets more product reads run at once, so fewer are refused under load, but lets reads hold more database connections that orders also need while Redis is down; the limit is a trade-off point.

ADR 0003 moves the payment gateway's API key and the money rows (payments table) out of DonHang.Api into DonHang.Payments, with its own database, deployed and granted access separately, joined to the api by a saga.

ADR 0003 consequences (lines 40-43): order and refund agree only after a while (order refunding, Payments row pending); one more service with its database, image and dashboard; every step must be safely repeatable since a message can arrive twice.

ADR 0003's gain is in its context and decision (outside the excerpt): key and money rows in one service of their own. YC-7 (answer within 2 s even when the gateway fails) comes from replying before the gateway is called, already done in refund design v1 inside DonHang.Api.

claims.text: The comment on Program.cs lines 145-146 names both sides: product reads need a database connection when Redis is down, and orders need them too.

Naming trade-off points tells the team which decisions to revisit when a driver changes and what each change costs elsewhere; in Đơn Hàng a PR moving one should not be approved on passing tests alone but say which attribute it favours and what the other loses.

Trade-offs table: unnamed points are cheap but break silently; naming next to the decision costs a sentence; a scenario or check per side is worth its upkeep when both sides matter and the point is likely to move.

Showing an order as refunded at once would make the request wait for the gateway to return the money; refund-design.md rejected calling the gateway in the customer's request because YC-7 fails when the gateway does. Keep answering with refunding unless the decider accepts losing YC-7.

claims.text: Misconceptions: no design is best at every attribute when attributes share a resource; a limit can be an architecture decision; a trade-off point is right only for the drivers it was set under (catalog-reads numbers, ADR 0003's separate service) and needs revisiting when they change.

Program.cs lines 135-141: the orders policy allows PermitLimit orders per fixed Window per customer, 10 per 1 minute unless configured, keyed by the access token's sub claim, which names the user the token was issued for.
A request refused by the fixed-window orders limit gets 429 (with Retry-After), set by the OnRejected handler.
